prompt: Which statements describe how Redis Software handles its default certificates?
explanation: The cluster autogenerates a set of self-signed certificates on the first node and copies that same set to every node that joins, and each certificate can later be replaced with one signed by a CA of your choice. The certificates are never signed by a public CA out of the box (which is why browsers show an untrusted warning), and the set covers several purposes — proxy, Cluster Manager UI, REST API, syncer, metrics exporter — so it is not just one shared certificate per node.

options.text: Self-signed certificates are autogenerated on the first node of the installation
The generated certificates are copied to every node that joins the cluster
Any autogenerated certificate can be replaced with one signed by a certificate authority
The certificates are signed by a public CA, so browsers trust them without any action
Each node generates its own unrelated certificate set during installation
